title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Cohort 3: Apply for the 7-Week UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity
summary: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Are you passionate about Africa’s development, leadership, public policy, education, entrepreneurship, community development, or the long-term vision of The Africa We Want ? The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers an opportunity to take part in a structured seven-week online learning and volunteer experience designed to help participants understand how they can contribute to Africa’s transformation within their own spheres of influence. Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and delivered through the wider Agenda 2063 learning ecosystem, the programme focuses on turning knowledge of Agenda 2063 into practical individual leadership and action. The online assignment is designed for people who want to explore their personal contribution to Africa’s development while supporting other participants during the seven-week traineeship. It does not require applicants to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. Instead, it emphasizes curiosity, critical engagement, communication, willingness to learn, and the ability to help others connect ideas to their own real-world environments. Opportunity Overview Opportunity Title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Host Entity: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Assignment Country: Ethiopia Modality: Online Duration: 7 weeks Time Commitment: 11–15 hours per week Task Type: Development of plans Relevant Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals Expected Start Date: The listing does not provide a valid start date Number of Assignments: 0 as indicated in the provided listing Language: English, fluent level desirable Deadline: No application deadline is specified in the provided opportunity details What Is Agenda 2063? Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development framework and vision for building “The Africa We Want.” It provides a continental framework for transforming Africa economically, socially and politically while promoting inclusive development, sustainable growth, integration and stronger partnerships. However, understanding Agenda 2063 as a policy or development framework is only one part of the challenge. Its implementation also depends on the actions of individuals and institutions operating in different environments. This is the central idea behind Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces . The programme recognizes that important decisions are made every day in many different environments, including: Governments and public institutions Businesses and private-sector organizations Universities and research institutions Schools and educational organizations Communities and civil society Development organizations Families Professional networks Entrepreneurship and innovation spaces Youth organizations Other environments where people make decisions and create value These environments are described as “Power Spaces.” The programme encourages participants to identify the Power Spaces available to them and consider how they can deliberately use those spaces to contribute to Africa’s long-term transformation. What Is Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3? Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is a seven-week online traineeship and volunteer learning experience designed to move participants beyond simply knowing about Agenda 2063. The programme seeks to help participants answer an important question: How can I personally contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the spaces in which I have influence? Rather than treating leadership as something limited to senior government officials, executives or institutional leaders, the programme takes a broader approach. It recognizes that individuals can create value and influence outcomes from wherever they operate. A student can influence a university or student organization. An entrepreneur can influence a business ecosystem. A teacher can influence learners and communities. A researcher can influence policy and knowledge. A community leader can influence local development. A communications professional can influence public awareness and engagement. The programme therefore focuses on developing individual agency and helping participants recognize themselves as potential contributors to Agenda 2063. Main Objective of the Programme The central objective is to help participants progress from understanding Agenda 2063 to recognizing themselves as agents capable of contributing to its implementation . The seven-week journey provides a structured framework through which participants examine: The value they currently create. The future they want to help create. The changes required to move from the present toward that future. The leadership values required to make meaningful decisions. The routines needed to turn intentions into action. The future they want to experience as a result of their efforts. The lessons they gain and the changes they need to make going forward. This makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in leadership, development practice, public policy, entrepreneurship, education, community development and African transformation. The Seven Leadership Tools Participants Will Develop One of the most important features of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is its seven-tool leadership architecture. Throughout the seven-week journey, participants progressively work with seven leadership tools. 1. Contribution Statement – What Value Do I Create? The first tool encourages participants to identify their personal contribution to Africa’s transformation. Participants examine their current Power Space and consider the value they create within it. This may involve asking questions such as: What am I currently contributing? Who benefits from my contribution? What capabilities do I possess? What problems am I helping to solve? Where do I have influence? How does my work or activity connect with Africa’s broader development needs? The Contribution Statement helps participants understand where they currently fit within the broader transformation agenda. 2. Moonshot – What Future Am I Committed to Creating? The second tool focuses on developing a sufficiently ambitious vision for the future. The concept of a “Moonshot” encourages participants to think beyond incremental improvements and identify a consequential future they are committed to helping create. Participants consider: What future do I want to see? What would meaningful transformation look like? What ambitious outcome would challenge current assumptions? What future is worth working toward despite present obstacles? The exercise is intended to help participants challenge the limitations imposed by present circumstances. 3. Delivery – What Must Change? Having identified a desired future, participants then examine what needs to change to move toward it. The Delivery tool focuses on the gap between the current situation and the desired outcome. Participants may consider: What is preventing progress? Which systems, behaviours or practices need to change? What obstacles must be addressed? Which changes are most critical? What actions can contribute to the desired transformation? This stage helps translate vision into a practical understanding of what needs to happen. 4. Leadership Values – Who Must I Be? The fourth tool focuses on the personal qualities and values required to pursue meaningful change. Participants reflect on the type of leader they need to become in order to make consequential decisions and remain committed to their goals. This can involve examining: Personal values Integrity Responsibility Courage Accountability Resilience Collaboration Commitment Respect for others Willingness to learn and adapt The emphasis is not simply on what participants want to achieve but also on who they need to be throughout the journey. 5. Leadership Routines – What Must I Repeatedly Do? A vision only becomes meaningful when it is translated into consistent action. The Leadership Routines tool helps participants identify repeated behaviours and practices that can gradually produce results. Participants consider: What actions must I perform consistently? Which habits will support my goals? What behaviours need to become routine? How can I turn intention into practice? What repeated actions can accumulate into meaningful results? This stage emphasizes the importance of sustained action rather than one-time motivation. 6. Letter from the Future – What Does Life Look Like Because I Succeeded? The sixth tool asks participants to imagine their desired future as though they have already achieved it. Through a Letter from the Future , participants explore what life looks like because their efforts succeeded. This exercise can help participants: Visualize the impact of their contribution. Understand the consequences of achieving their goals. Reconsider current choices. Identify actions that are consistent with their desired future. Strengthen their connection to their long-term objectives. The exercise links future aspirations with present-day decision-making. 7. Future Review – What Have I Learned and What Should I Now Revise? The final tool focuses on reflection, learning and continuous improvement. Participants are introduced to the practice of: Return → Review → Revise → Recommit This process encourages participants to revisit their leadership plans and assess whether their circumstances, experiences and capabilities have changed. Instead of treating the seven-week programme as an endpoint, participants are encouraged to continue applying the tools after the formal traineeship ends. What Will Online Volunteers Do? Online Volunteers will play a supporting role throughout the seven-week traineeship. Their responsibilities will include the following. Study the Learning Materials Volunteers will become familiar with the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces learning materials, including the Reader and associated resources. This requires participants to: Read the provided materials. Understand the major concepts. Engage critically with the learning content. Prepare to support participant learning. Develop familiarity with the seven leadership tools. Volunteers are not expected to arrive as experts. The assignment specifically emphasizes curiosity and disciplined engagement with the materials. Support Participant Engagement Volunteers will help support participants throughout the seven-week learning journey. This involves understanding the weekly concepts, questions and exercises and helping participants remain engaged with the programme. The emphasis is on supporting learning rather than simply delivering course content. Participate in Small-Group Learning Conversations Where assigned, volunteers will participate in small-group conversations. These discussions are intended to encourage participants to connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces. Volunteers should therefore be capable of: Listening actively. Encouraging participation. Asking constructive questions. Helping participants connect concepts to their own experiences. Providing concise and useful feedback. Supporting a collaborative learning environment. Contribute to the End-of-Cohort Review Volunteers will also participate in a structured review at the end of the cohort. They will help identify: What worked well. What challenges participants experienced. What could be improved. Which learning approaches were effective. How future cohorts could be strengthened. How the materials and participant experience could be improved. This means volunteers can contribute not only to the current cohort but also to the continued development of the programme. Who Can Apply? The opportunity welcomes applications from people with an interest in Africa’s transformation and related areas. The requirements specifically mention applicants from a variety of professional and educational backgrounds, including: Professionals Development practitioners Researchers Entrepreneurs Educators Students Community leaders Applicants may come from different sectors and Power Spaces. The programme is therefore not restricted to one profession or academic discipline. Required Experience and Skills Candidates should be able to demonstrate a strong interest in one or more areas connected to Agenda 2063 and African development. Relevant areas include: Agenda 2063 African development Leadership Development practice Public policy Business Education Community development Related fields Applicants should also demonstrate the following capabilities. Critical Reading and Learning Candidates should be comfortable reading learning materials and engaging with them critically. The programme requires volunteers to understand concepts sufficiently to support discussions and participant engagement. Strong Written Communication Good written communication is important because volunteers may need to provide feedback, participate in discussions and communicate ideas clearly. Strong Interpersonal Communication The role involves interaction with other participants, particularly through small-group learning conversations. Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating respectfully and constructively with people from different backgrounds. Constructive Feedback Volunteers should be able to provide feedback that is: Concise Clear Constructive Relevant Helpful to the learning process Commitment Applicants must be able to commit to the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period. The expected workload is 11–15 hours per week , making it important for applicants to assess their availability before applying. Language Requirement The listed language requirement is: English – Fluent, desirable. Applicants should therefore be able to comfortably understand and engage with English-language learning materials and participate effectively in written and interpersonal communication. Programme Modality and Time Commitment The assignment is conducted entirely online . This makes it suitable for participants who can contribute remotely without needing to relocate to Ethiopia or another physical programme location. The expected commitment is: 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks. Applicants should ensure they have sufficient time to: Study the learning materials. Participate in learning conversations. Support participant engagement. Complete assigned activities. Contribute to the end-of-cohort review. What Makes This Opportunity Different? One of the distinctive features of the programme is that it does not simply present Agenda 2063 as something participants should know. Instead, it asks participants to consider how they can personally contribute to its implementation. This approach is important because continental transformation depends not only on governments and large institutions but also on the decisions and actions taken in everyday environments. The programme s Power Spaces approach recognizes that individuals have different forms of influence. A participant does not necessarily need to occupy a senior position to contribute to development. Their influence could come through: Their profession Their organization Their business Their research Their classroom Their community Their professional network Their family Their youth or civic activities Their educational institution This makes the programme relevant to participants at different stages of their careers and lives. Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future Participants are expected to retain important outputs from the learning journey, including their Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future . These materials can serve as practical references after the seven-week programme. Rather than treating leadership development as a one-time training activity, the programme encourages participants to revisit their materials periodically as their circumstances, experience, capabilities and Power Spaces evolve. This creates an opportunity for continuous reflection and development. Contribution to Future Cohorts Another important aspect of Cohort 3 is its contribution to the continued improvement of the programme. Participants and volunteers will help test and improve: Learning materials Facilitation approaches Participant engagement methods Overall learning experience Approaches for making the leadership practice accessible to larger numbers of people Consequently, participation can contribute to the development of future iterations of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces. Connection to Sustainable Development Goal 17 The assignment is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals . SDG 17 emphasizes the importance of partnerships in achieving sustainable development. The connection is particularly relevant because Agenda 2063 implementation requires collaboration among governments, businesses, communities, civil society, educational institutions, development organizations and individuals. By encouraging people to identify their Power Spaces and collaborate across different environments, the programme reinforces the importance of partnerships in achieving long-term development objectives. Is This a Paid Opportunity? The provided description identifies this as an online volunteer assignment . It specifically explains that volunteerism involves activities undertaken freely for the public good where monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor. Therefore, applicants should not approach this as a paid employment opportunity . The programme is better suited to individuals interested in learning, leadership development, contribution to African development, collaboration and volunteer experience. Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity The programme states that United Nations Volunteers is an equal opportunity programme that welcomes qualified applicants. It is committed to diversity and respect for human rights and individual dignity. The inclusivity statement specifies that discrimination should not occur on the basis of characteristics including: Race Sex Gender identity Religion Nationality Ethnic origin Sexual orientation Disability Pregnancy Age Language Social origin Other status The programme therefore emphasizes an inclusive environment in which qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds can participate. Who Is the Ideal Candidate? The ideal candidate is someone who is genuinely interested in contributing to Africa s long-term development and is willing to learn rather than simply demonstrate existing expertise. A strong applicant could be someone who: Has an interest in Agenda 2063 and African development. Is passionate about leadership and positive change. Can critically read and understand learning materials. Communicates clearly in English. Works effectively with other people. Can provide constructive feedback. Is comfortable participating in online learning. Can dedicate 11–15 hours every week for seven weeks. Is open to learning from people with different experiences. Can connect abstract ideas with real-world contexts. Is willing to reflect on their own contribution and leadership. Wants to continue applying the programme s tools beyond the formal traineeship. Benefits of Participating Although the opportunity is a volunteer assignment rather than a paid position, participants can gain several forms of professional and personal value. Leadership Development The seven-tool framework provides participants with a structured approach to examining their contribution, aspirations, values, routines and future goals. Understanding of Agenda 2063 Participants gain an opportunity to engage directly with Agenda 2063 and explore its relevance to individual action and African transformation. Practical Reflection The programme goes beyond theoretical learning by encouraging participants to apply the concepts to their own Power Spaces. Collaboration Small-group learning conversations provide opportunities to engage with people from different professional, educational and community backgrounds. Communication Skills Supporting discussions and providing constructive feedback can strengthen written and interpersonal communication. Development Perspective The programme can help participants connect individual leadership with broader development objectives. International Volunteer Experience Participation in an online UN-linked volunteer assignment can provide experience of contributing to an international development-oriented initiative. How to Prepare for the Opportunity Applicants interested in this programme should carefully consider how their existing experience connects with the assignment. Before applying, it can be useful to reflect on the following questions: What does Agenda 2063 mean to me? What aspect of African development interests me most? What Power Space do I currently operate in? What value do I create in that space? What development challenge would I like to help address? What leadership qualities do I already demonstrate? What leadership qualities do I need to strengthen? Can I dedicate 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks? Can I effectively communicate and collaborate with people online? How could my professional, academic, entrepreneurial or community experience contribute to the programme? Applicants should also ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their motivation, relevant interests, communication abilities and commitment. Important Scam Warning Applicants should be particularly careful about fraudulent individuals or websites claiming to represent the United Nations. The opportunity information explicitly warns that the United Nations does not charge application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or recruitment fees . If anyone requests money in exchange for applying, being shortlisted, receiving training or securing recruitment, applicants should disregard the request. Applicants should also exercise caution when submitting personal information online because logos, names, addresses and other organizational materials can be copied and reproduced by scammers. Always verify that an application is being submitted through the legitimate United Nations or UN Volunteers recruitment platform. Application Deadline No application deadline is specified in the opportunity information provided. Applicants should therefore check the official listing for the current application status and any deadline or closing date before submitting an application. The provided listing also shows an invalid/unspecified expected start date , so applicants should verify the latest programme schedule through the official recruitment platform. APPLY HERE Conclusion The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 provides an opportunity to engage with Africa s long-term development vision from a personal and practical leadership perspective. Its central message is that achieving The Africa We Want is not solely the responsibility of governments or major institutions. Transformation can also emerge from the many Power Spaces in which individuals learn, work, build businesses, conduct research, educate others, participate in communities and make decisions. Over seven weeks, participants will explore seven practical leadership tools covering contribution, vision, delivery, values, routines, future thinking and continuous review. They will also support other learners, participate in group conversations and contribute feedback that can improve future cohorts. For professionals, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, educators, practitioners and community leaders interested in Africa s development, this online volunteer assignment can provide a structured opportunity to deepen their understanding of Agenda 2063 while reflecting on how their own work and influence can contribute to the continent s transformation. With a commitment of 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks , applicants should ensure that they have sufficient time and motivation to participate fully. Most importantly, successful participation requires more than familiarity with development terminology. It requires curiosity, critical thinking, communication, collaboration and a genuine willingness to connect ideas with action. The programme ultimately encourages participants to move from asking “What is Agenda 2063?” toward a more personal and consequential question: “What can I contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the Power Spaces available to me?” For more global volunteering opportunity visit OFY HERE. title: CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship 2026
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is offering a research and training opportunity through the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) for qualified researchers and graduate-level professionals interested in physical activity promotion, public health, community design, implementation science, epidemiology, data analysis, policy, and related fields. The CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship , referenced as CDC-2026-0033 , provides an opportunity for an eligible participant to train with CDC s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP) , specifically within the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity (DNPAO) in Atlanta, Georgia. This fellowship is particularly relevant to individuals interested in using scientific research, data, policy, community partnerships, and evidence-based interventions to increase physical activity and improve public health outcomes. About the CDC Physical Activty Fellowship The fellowship is connected to Active People, Healthy Nation , a national CDC initiative designed to help 27 million Americans become more physically active by 2027 . The initiative recognizes physical activity as an important component of population health and seeks to create environments and systems that make physical activity easier and more accessible. As an ORISE participant, the selected fellow will work alongside multidisciplinary teams at CDC and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The training experience will involve research, evidence translation, partnership development, communication, evaluation, policy analysis, and dissemination activities related to physical activity promotion. A major area of focus is activity-friendly community design . This involves identifying, evaluating, and communicating evidence-based approaches that increase opportunities for people to: Walk Bicycle Use public transportation Access everyday destinations through active transportation Engage in other forms of routine physical activity The fellowship therefore goes beyond traditional exercise promotion. It examines how communities, transportation systems, policies, urban environments, and public health strategies can be designed to support healthier and more physically active populations. Research Project The selected ORISE participant will be placed within CDC s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion , in the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity . The research and training experience will contribute to nationally significant public health initiatives that aim to generate, interpret, translate, and communicate scientific evidence. The fellow will contribute to efforts supporting Active People, Healthy Nation and may participate in activities involving: Scientific research Evidence reviews Implementation science Evaluation Policy analysis Data analysis Community-level strategies Evidence translation Scientific writing Dissemination Partnership development Public health communication The fellow will also have opportunities to work with experts and organizations across several disciplines, creating an interdisciplinary training environment. Key Learning Objectives One of the strongest features of this fellowship is the breadth of professional and research skills participants can develop. Under the supervision and guidance of experienced mentors, the selected fellow will have opportunities to develop the following competencies. 1. Scientific Evidence Reviews The participant will learn how to support scientific evidence reviews, coordination, and communication activities that may contribute to future updates of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd Edition . This experience can provide valuable exposure to the process of reviewing scientific evidence and translating research findings into public health guidance. 2. National Partnership Development The fellow will learn how to engage with national partners in support of updates to the National Physical Activity Plan . This can involve working with organizations and stakeholders whose activities influence physical activity, health promotion, community development, transportation, and related areas. 3. Scientific Writing and Publications The fellowship provides opportunities to develop experience in authoring or co-authoring: Peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts Scientific reports Conference presentations Evidence summaries Other scientific communication products This is particularly valuable for candidates interested in establishing or strengthening a research and academic career. 4. Implementation Science Participants will build knowledge and skills in implementation science , which focuses on understanding how evidence-based interventions, programs, and policies can be effectively translated into real-world practice. This may include examining why certain interventions work in particular communities and how successful strategies can be implemented or scaled. 5. Evaluation and Dissemination Research The fellow will have opportunities to gain experience in evaluation and dissemination research. These skills are important in determining whether public health programs and strategies are achieving their intended objectives and how evidence can be effectively communicated to organizations, policymakers, professionals, and communities. 6. Policy Analysis The fellowship includes opportunities to understand policy analysis and evaluation related to community design and physical activity promotion. This can involve examining how policies and community-level decisions influence opportunities for physical activity. 7. Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis Participants will learn to apply both quantitative and qualitative analytical methods. Depending on project needs, this may include working with: Statistical data Qualitative data Mixed-method approaches R Python GIS Spatial analysis Emerging analytical approaches Candidates with existing data-analysis experience may therefore find this opportunity particularly relevant. 8. Interdisciplinary Collaboration The fellow will work in interdisciplinary groups and interact with professionals from fields such as: Public health Physical activity Tribal health Urban planning Epidemiology Community planning Transportation planning Policy Research This provides an opportunity to understand public health problems from multiple professional perspectives. 9. Qualitative Research The participant will build skills in qualitative methodology, including opportunities related to qualitative data collection, methodology, and analysis. 10. Data Analysis and Evidence Translation The fellowship will provide opportunities to analyze data and translate scientific findings into products that can be understood and used by different audiences. Participants may contribute to manuscripts and other materials addressing physical activity and community-level interventions. 11. Public Health Communication The fellow will gain experience developing materials such as: Infographics Fact sheets Evidence summaries Messaging materials Other communication products These materials may be designed for policymakers, public health professionals, leadership, professionals in other sectors, and the general public. 12. Presentation Skills Participants will also develop their ability to prepare and deliver presentations to internal and external audiences. This can strengthen communication skills that are essential for researchers and public health professionals. Preferred Skills and Experience Although the opportunity has specific eligibility requirements, CDC has also identified several preferred skills that can strengthen an applicant s profile. The preferred candidate may have experience in: Strong oral and written communication Scientific writing Peer-reviewed publications Scientific reports Scientific communication Teamwork Partner engagement Physical activity Active transportation Land-use planning Parks and recreation Related public health sectors Qualitative data Qualitative research methodology Qualitative data analysis Translating scientific findings into plain language R Python Tribal organizations and communities Implementation science Evaluation methods Mixed-methods research GIS/spatial analysis Community planning Transportation planning Data visualization Applicants do not necessarily need to possess every preferred skill. The fellowship is designed as a training experience, and candidates should highlight the relevant skills and experiences they already possess. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The opportunity has a specific eligibility requirement that applicants should carefully review before beginning an application. Citizenship Requirement The fellowship is available to U.S. citizens only . This means that individuals who are citizens of other countries but do not hold U.S. citizenship are not eligible for this particular opportunity. There is no race or ethnicity restriction stated in the eligibility requirements. However, the citizenship requirement is mandatory. Academic Requirement Applicants must have: A master s degree , or A doctoral degree in one of the eligible disciplines. The degree must have been received within the previous 60 months . Alternatively, applicants who are currently pursuing a qualifying master s or doctoral degree may be eligible if they anticipate graduating by January 27, 2027 . Eligible Academic Disciplines The listed eligible disciplines fall into two broad categories: Life, Health and Medical Sciences Applicants with relevant academic backgrounds within the life, health, and medical sciences may qualify, depending on how their degree aligns with the fellowship s requirements. Social and Behavioral Sciences Applicants from relevant social and behavioral science disciplines may also qualify. Because the fellowship focuses on physical activity, public health, community design, policy, implementation, evaluation, and behavioral and population-level interventions, candidates should carefully demonstrate how their academic background connects with the fellowship s research objectives. Where Is the Fellowship Located? The research opportunity is based at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, Georgia, USA . The fellow will participate in a full-time training appointment and work with CDC and HHS teams involved in physical activity and public health initiatives. Fellowship Duration The appointment is initially expected to last one year . However, the appointment may be renewed upon the recommendation of CDC and depending on the availability of funding. The anticipated start date is listed as September 31, 2026 , although the opportunity states that the start date is flexible and will depend on several factors. Applicants should note that September has only 30 days. Therefore, the stated September 31 date appears to be a date-entry inconsistency in the announcement, and applicants should rely on the official application information or contact the listed point of contact if the exact start date is important to their application. Learn More About This Opportunity HERE Level of Participation This is a full-time appointment. The selected participant will therefore be expected to devote full-time participation to the fellowship and its research and training activities. Participant Stipend The fellowship provides a participant stipend . However, the announcement does not provide one fixed stipend amount. The stipend rate may vary according to several factors, including: The specific opportunity Location Educational background Experience Other applicable factors Candidates who reach the interview stage may ask about the exact stipend rate. If selected, the official appointment offer will state the applicable monthly stipend. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a specific dollar amount unless it is provided directly by ORISE or in their appointment offer. Health Insurance and Participant Status ORISE participants do not become employees of CDC, the U.S. Department of Energy, or ORAU . The fellowship also does not provide traditional employment-related benefits associated with being a CDC employee. Proof of health insurance is required for participation. Health insurance may be obtained through ORISE. Prospective applicants should therefore understand that this is a structured research and training appointment rather than a standard CDC employment position. Environmental, Safety and Health Requirements Successful applicants will be required to comply with the environmental, safety, and health requirements applicable to the hosting facility. These requirements may include health and safety measures established by the facility, including applicable COVID-19-related requirements such as: Facial covering Physical distancing Testing Vaccination Applicants should be prepared to comply with the requirements applicable at the time of their appointment. How to Apply A complete application must contain all required components. Applicants should prepare the following: 1. Application Form Complete and submit the official application through the designated ORISE application system. Apply HERE 2. Academic Transcripts Applicants must provide the required transcripts. The announcement specifies that applicants should review the detailed ORISE transcript guidelines to determine what constitutes an acceptable transcript. If documents are not in English, an official English translation must be included. 3. Current Resume or CV The resume/CV should be current and should clearly present relevant academic and professional experience. It should include information such as: Academic history Employment history Relevant research or professional experience Publications, where applicable Relevant technical skills Other experiences related to the fellowship Candidates should tailor their CV to the research focus rather than submitting a generic resume whenever possible. 4. Recommendation Applicants must provide one educational or professional recommendation . This is an important requirement. The application will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed until at least one recommendation has been submitted. Applicants should therefore contact their recommender early enough to ensure the recommendation is submitted before the application is reviewed. Language Requirement All application documents must be submitted in English . If an applicant s documents are in another language, they must include an official English translation . This requirement applies particularly to academic documents and other materials submitted as part of the application. Application Deadline The application deadline is: September 11, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Time. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis . Because applications may be reviewed before the final deadline, applicants should not wait until September 11 to submit their materials. A strong strategy is to prepare the CV, transcripts, recommendation, and other application materials well in advance and submit a complete application as early as possible.. Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable This opportunity offers more than a traditional academic research placement. A successful participant could gain exposure to the way a major U.S. public health agency uses research evidence to influence programs, policies, community strategies, and public health communication. Some of the major professional development areas include: Public health research Scientific writing Evidence synthesis Policy analysis Implementation science Evaluation Data analysis Qualitative research GIS and spatial analysis Scientific communication Public health messaging Community design Active transportation Partnership development Interdisciplinary collaboration Conference presentations Peer-reviewed publications For researchers interested in population health and physical activity, the fellowship could provide an opportunity to work at the intersection of science, policy, community planning, and public health practice . Who Should Consider Applying? This fellowship may be particularly suitable for eligible U.S. citizens who are pursuing or have recently completed graduate-level education in areas connected to health, medicine, life sciences, social sciences, behavioral sciences, public health, epidemiology, or related disciplines. Candidates with experience in any of the following areas may find the opportunity especially relevant: Public health Epidemiology Physical activity research Health promotion Behavioral science Community health Implementation science Program evaluation Qualitative research Quantitative research Mixed-methods research Urban planning Transportation planning GIS Data science Policy analysis Health communication Scientific writing The strongest applicants should demonstrate not only academic qualifications but also an ability to work collaboratively, communicate scientific findings, analyze information, and connect research evidence with real-world public health practice. Application Preparation Tips Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should carefully check that their materials demonstrate a clear connection between their background and the fellowship. Tailor your CV Emphasize research, publications, data analysis, public health projects, community work, presentations, and other experiences relevant to the fellowship. Demonstrate research skills If you have experience with R, Python, GIS, qualitative research, quantitative analysis, mixed methods, or data visualization, make those skills easy for reviewers to identify. Highlight scientific communication Publications, research reports, conference presentations, policy briefs, infographics, fact sheets, and other communication products can demonstrate your ability to translate evidence for different audiences. Connect your experience to physical activity Experience involving physical activity, active transportation, community planning, parks, land use, health promotion, or related sectors can be particularly valuable. Secure your recommendation early Because the application will not be reviewed until a recommendation has been submitted, applicants should not leave this requirement until the last minute. Apply early The opportunity uses rolling review. Submitting a complete application early may therefore be preferable to waiting until the final deadline. CONCLUSION The CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship is a specialized research and training opportunity for eligible U.S. citizens with a recent or forthcoming master s or doctoral degree in a relevant discipline. The fellowship combines public health research, physical activity promotion, community design, policy analysis, implementation science, evaluation, data analysis, scientific writing, and evidence translation . Participants will have the opportunity to work with multidisciplinary professionals while contributing to initiatives connected to CDC s Active People, Healthy Nation campaign. With a full-time initial appointment of one year, a participant stipend, opportunities for professional development, and potential exposure to peer-reviewed research and national public health initiatives, the fellowship can be particularly valuable for graduate-level researchers seeking experience in applied public health science. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The opportunity is restricted to U.S. citizens , requires a qualifying master s or doctoral degree obtained within the past 60 months or anticipated by January 27, 2027 , and requires a complete application containing the application form, transcripts, current CV/resume, and at least one educational or professional recommendation. Most importantly, applicants should remember the September 11, 2026, 3:00 PM Eastern Time deadline and the fact that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Preparing and submitting a complete, carefully tailored application early can help ensure that the application is available for consideration. title: African Nutrition Leadership Programme (ANLP) 2027: Apply for the 10-Day Nutrition Leadership Development Programme in Africa
summary: The African Nutrition Leadership Programme (ANLP) is a leadership development initiative focused on strengthening nutrition leadership capacity across the African continent. Based at North-West University in South Africa , the programme works to develop the leadership abilities of early- and mid-career nutrition professionals and other stakeholders whose work contributes to improving nutrition and health outcomes in Africa. The ANLP has been successfully delivering its flagship 10-day Leadership Development Programme since 2002 , bringing together professionals from a broad range of nutrition-related disciplines and sectors. Through an intensive leadership development experience, the programme aims to equip participants with the knowledge, skills, perspectives and leadership capabilities needed to contribute more effectively to nutrition programmes, policies, institutions and initiatives across Africa. Applications and further information are available for the 2027 ANLP programme . title: UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026: Home-Based Opportunity for Disaster Risk Reduction and AI Enthusiasts
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for its Early Warning Preparedness Internship 2026 , a six-month, home-based internship supporting the organisation’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team (DRT). This opportunity is particularly relevant for students and recent graduates interested in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, humanitarian affairs, risk intelligence, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, early warning systems, and resilience building . The internship will provide an opportunity to contribute to UNDP’s work on risk intelligence, preparedness, anticipation, and the use of digital and AI-powered technologies for disaster risk reduction. The successful intern will also support research, knowledge management, learning, and communications activities within the UNDP Crisis Bureau. UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship 2026 at a Glance Organisation: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Position: Early Warning Preparedness Intern Job Identification: 35990 Location: Home-Based Contract Duration: 6 months Job Type: Full-time internship Practice Area: Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Grade: IN Application Deadline: 1 September 2026 at 4:45 PM Working Language: English Other UN Languages: Knowledge of another UN official language is an asset. About the UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship UNDP works with governments and partners at international, national, and local levels to reduce disaster risks, strengthen resilience, and promote development that is risk-informed and sustainable. The Early Warning Preparedness Internship forms part of this broader effort. The intern will contribute to activities involving risk intelligence, early warning, preparedness, anticipation, digital innovation, and artificial intelligence applications for disaster risk reduction . The role combines research, analysis, technology, knowledge management, learning, and communications. This makes it particularly suitable for candidates who want to understand how emerging technologies and evidence-based approaches can be applied to real-world disaster and development challenges. What Will the UNDP Intern Do? The selected intern will support several areas of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team s work. 1. Risk Intelligence and Digital Innovation A major component of the internship involves researching emerging developments in risk intelligence and digital technologies. The intern may be expected to: Conduct research and analysis on emerging trends, methodologies, tools, and best practices in risk intelligence and disaster risk reduction. Explore developments in artificial intelligence, geospatial technologies, digital public infrastructure, and data ecosystems relevant to disaster risk reduction. Support the continued development of UNDP’s Risk Intelligence Service Line. Identify innovative approaches and document lessons learned. Contribute to the development of service packages and value propositions. Map and analyse AI-powered and digital applications relevant to risk intelligence. Research technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, risk modelling, early warning systems, and data visualisation. Develop knowledge products, concept notes, guidance materials, case studies, policy briefs, and communications products. Identify opportunities for applying innovative digital technologies within UNDP programming. This aspect of the internship is particularly valuable for applicants interested in the intersection of AI, data, technology, disaster preparedness, and international development . 2. Knowledge Sharing and Country-Level Good Practices The intern will also help identify and communicate successful approaches being implemented by UNDP Country Offices, Regional Hubs and partners. Responsibilities may include: Documenting country-level good practices. Identifying innovative solutions in disaster risk reduction and preparedness. Supporting dissemination of lessons and experiences. Engaging with technical institutions, research organisations, technology providers, UN entities, and academic institutions. Contributing to presentations and briefing notes. Supporting donor materials and proposals. Contributing to strategic documents related to partnerships and resource mobilisation. Through these activities, the intern can gain exposure to how international development organisations collect, package, and communicate knowledge to governments, partners, donors, and other stakeholders. 3. Preparedness Learning Pathway Another important part of the internship is supporting the continued development of UNDP’s Preparedness Learning Pathway . The intern will assist with: Researching and categorising resources for the expansion and tailoring of the corporate learning package. Supporting the development and maintenance of the online Preparedness Learning Pathway repository. Contributing to a self-paced course under the UNDP Crisis Academy. Researching resources for new thematic modules of the UNDP Preparedness Toolkit. This provides exposure to learning and knowledge-management processes within a major international development organisation. 4. Webinars, Learning Activities, and Digital Engagement The intern will also support webinars and related learning activities. Tasks may include: Preparing webinar plans. Developing facilitation guidance. Supporting MURAL boards. Assisting with group discussions. Supporting Zoom arrangements. Preparing webinar reports. Supporting other learning activities. Contributing to serious game methodologies under the Preparedness Learning Pathway. Developing social media kits for workshops and webinars. Preparing presentations, talking points, and briefing notes relating to UNDP’s global early warning portfolio. Candidates with strong communication, digital collaboration, and content-development skills may therefore find this component especially relevant. 5. Research, Analysis, and Communications The internship also offers exposure to broader research and communications activities within the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team. The intern may contribute to research and analysis concerning: Urban resilience. Gender equality and women’s leadership in disaster risk reduction. Disaster risk financing. Funding and project proposals. Briefs and talking points. Presentations and slide decks. Knowledge management. Communications activities. Other research and analytical assignments as required. Who Can Apply for the UNDP Internship? Educational Qualifications Applicants must meet at least one of the specified educational requirements at the time of application. Eligible applicants include those who: Are enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme, such as a Master’s degree or higher , in: Disaster risk reduction; Climate change adaptation; Disaster management; or Humanitarian affairs. Are enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree , such as a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, in one of the relevant fields. Have recently graduated with a relevant university degree and, if selected, are able to begin the internship within one year of graduation. Are enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship programme and will undertake the internship as part of that programme. Required Skills and Experience Beyond academic qualifications, applicants should demonstrate a combination of communication, research, technology, and organisational skills. Important capabilities include: Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to write clearly and concisely. Good command of information and communication technology. Strong research and analytical abilities. Strong organisational skills. Excellent attention to detail. Proven proofreading ability. Ability to work with web-based applications. Familiarity with social media. Experience or familiarity with data management systems. Artificial Intelligence and Digital Skills The position also highlights familiarity with conversational AI applications such as: Copilot; Claude; ChatGPT; and Gemini. Knowledge of collaborative tools such as MURAL, Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Forms is also relevant. Knowledge of design applications such as Canva and Gamma is considered advantageous. This makes the opportunity particularly interesting for applicants who can combine academic knowledge in disaster-related fields with practical digital and communications skills. Core Competencies UNDP Is Looking For Successful candidates should demonstrate several important competencies. Initiative Applicants should be capable of working independently, identifying opportunities and taking appropriate action without requiring constant supervision. Collaboration The intern should be able to work effectively within a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment , which is essential in an international organisation such as the UNDP. Communication Strong written and verbal communication skills are required because the role involves research outputs, presentations, briefs, webinars, knowledge products, and communications materials. Attention to Detail The ability to produce accurate, clear, and well-structured work is important, particularly when preparing research, policy, and communications materials. Organisation The intern will potentially manage several assignments and priorities, making strong organisational and time-management abilities essential. Language Requirements Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of another UN official language is considered an asset. Applicants who possess additional UN language skills may therefore have an advantage, although English is the stated required language. What Benefits Does the UNDP Internship Offer? One of the notable features of this internship is the provision for financial support through a stipend. Where an intern is not financially supported by a university, government, foundation, scholarship programme or another institution , UNDP will provide a stipend intended to help cover basic daily expenses associated with the internship. The monthly amount will be determined according to applicable UNDP internship policies and duty-station rates. Where an external funding source provides financial support, UNDP may, subject to applicable rules, pay the difference between that support and the applicable UNDP stipend. Part-time arrangements are prorated where applicable. Interns will also accrue combined sick and annual leave at the applicable monthly rate, with part-time arrangements prorated where relevant. Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Your Career The UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship brings together several increasingly important areas of international development. Exposure to Disaster Risk Reduction The internship provides practical exposure to disaster risk reduction and preparedness work within a UN organisation. Experience With Emerging Technologies The role specifically touches on artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, risk modelling and data visualisation. International Development Experience Working with the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team provides an opportunity to understand how international development organisations support governments and partners in building resilience. Research and Analytical Development Interns can strengthen their ability to research emerging issues, analyse information, identify trends and turn findings into useful knowledge products. Communications Experience The position includes preparation of briefs, presentations, talking points, policy materials, social media kits, webinar reports, and other communications products. Knowledge Management and Learning The Preparedness Learning Pathway component can provide practical experience in organising resources, developing learning materials, and supporting online learning activities. Multicultural Collaboration The role involves collaboration within a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment, helping interns develop experience relevant to future careers in international organisations, development agencies, research institutions, and humanitarian organisations. What Documents Are Required When Applying? Applicants are required to submit: A brief cover letter in English explaining why they want to be considered for the internship. A current CV in English . Importantly, the cover letter and CV must be combined into one PDF document , because the application system permits only one document upload. Documents Successful Candidates May Need to Provide Candidates who are selected may subsequently be requested to provide electronic copies of supporting documentation, including: Most recent curriculum vitae. A letter from the university confirming current enrolment and graduation date, where applicable. Recent graduation certificate, where applicable. Letter of recommendation from a professor. School transcript. Passport. Medical Certificate of Good Health. Proof of medical insurance coverage. Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic and identification documents are readily available should they progress through the selection process. Application Deadline The deadline for the UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship is: 1 September 2026 at 4:45 PM. Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the final hours to avoid potential technical or submission-related difficulties. How to Apply for the UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship Interested and suitably qualified candidates should apply through the official UNDP recruitment portal for Job Identification 35990 . Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully review the eligibility requirements and ensure that their CV and cover letter clearly demonstrate their relevance to the internship. A strong application should make the connection between the applicant s: Academic background; Disaster risk reduction or related interests; Research and analytical abilities; Digital and technology skills; Communication capabilities; Knowledge-management experience; Relevant professional, volunteer, or academic projects; and Interest in UNDP s work on early warning and preparedness. APPLY HERE Additional Information About the Selection Process UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from the vacancy announcement. Applications may also be retained for consideration for other similar positions at the same grade level with comparable educational and experience requirements. Selected candidates will be subject to reference and background checks and will be expected to comply with UNDP standards and principles. The UNDP also maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. Who Qualifies for This Opportunity? Eligible category of people: Students, recent graduates, and postgraduate professional trainees whose academic or professional training is relevant to disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, or humanitarian affairs. Academic level The opportunity is open to candidates who are: In the final year of a relevant Bachelor’s degree; Enrolled in a relevant postgraduate programme such as a Master’s degree or higher; Recent graduates with a relevant degree, provided they can begin the internship within one year of graduation; or Participants in a relevant postgraduate professional traineeship programme. Nationality, race, and geographic eligibility The supplied opportunity information does not specify a particular race, nationality, country, region, or continent restriction . The vacancy is presented as a home-based, global opportunity , but applicants should confirm any nationality or location conditions directly in the official UNDP recruitment portal before applying. The source itself does not identify an exclusive eligible country or continent. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Applicants can strengthen their applications by tailoring their documents specifically to the responsibilities listed in the vacancy. 1. Tailor Your CV Instead of submitting a generic CV, highlight experience connected to: Disaster risk reduction; Climate change; Humanitarian affairs; Research and analysis; AI and digital technologies; Data management; Geospatial technologies; Communications; Knowledge management; Social media; Webinar coordination; and Development or humanitarian programming. 2. Connect Your Cover Letter to UNDP s Priorities The cover letter should clearly explain why the applicant is interested in early warning, preparedness, risk intelligence, and disaster risk reduction . Demonstrate Digital Competence Since the position highlights AI, digital applications, data ecosystems, and collaborative technologies, applicants should clearly identify relevant tools and projects they have worked with. Show Evidence of Research Ability Rather than simply stating excellent research skills, applicants should demonstrate research experience through academic projects, professional assignments, publications, reports, policy briefs, dissertations, or other relevant work. 5. Highlight Communication Skills The role involves numerous communications outputs. Conclusion The UNDP Early Warning Preparedness Internship 2026 presents an opportunity for students, recent graduates, and professional trainees to gain practical experience at the intersection of disaster risk reduction, early warning, preparedness, artificial intelligence, digital innovation, research, knowledge management, and international development .
