title: STEM Pathways Fund 2026: Up to £150,000 in Grants to Help Young People Transition from Further Education into STEM Careers
summary: The STEM Pathways Fund 2026 is a major funding opportunity designed to support organisations helping disadvantaged young people in Further Education (FE) across England successfully transition into science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) careers, apprenticeships, higher education and technical training. The fund is particularly focused on young people aged 16–19 who face financial, social, educational, structural or other barriers that can make it difficult to progress from Further Education into meaningful STEM opportunities. Through this pilot fund, Mission 44 and Santander UK Foundation aim to support a small portfolio of organisations developing practical, sustained and collaborative approaches to improving STEM transitions. Successful organisations could receive grants ranging from £75,000 to £150,000 for projects lasting up to 24 months . The fund is intended not only to improve individual outcomes for young people but also to generate learning that can contribute to stronger, more equitable Further Education and employment systems. Opportunity Category Category: Grant What Is the STEM Pathways Fund? The transition from education into employment, further study or training represents a critical stage in a young person s development. For young people experiencing disadvantage, however, this transition can be particularly difficult. The STEM Pathways Fund has been created in response to the barriers faced by young people in Further Education who may struggle to access clear career pathways, professional networks, careers guidance, work experience, role models and other opportunities that can help them make informed decisions about their futures. The fund recognises that Further Education plays an important role in developing the UK s future STEM workforce. Around 1.7 million young people aged 16–19 study in Further Education settings in England , with a substantial proportion coming from disadvantaged backgrounds. However, pressures on the FE sector can limit the capacity of colleges and other organisations to provide the sustained careers guidance, employer engagement and transition support that young people need. The STEM Pathways Fund therefore seeks to invest in organisations that can strengthen these pathways and help young people move successfully into: STEM employment STEM apprenticeships Degree apprenticeships Higher education Higher technical qualifications Vocational STEM qualifications Specialist STEM training Other recognised education, training or employment opportunities leading towards STEM careers The Problem the Fund Seeks to Address Many young people in Further Education encounter multiple barriers during their journey from education into employment or further study. These barriers can occur at several critical transition points. 1. Entry into Further Education At around age 16, young people are often required to make important decisions about their education and future careers. Without access to high-quality careers guidance, trusted advice and clear information, choosing the right post-16 pathway can be confusing. Young people may not fully understand: The range of STEM careers available The qualifications required for different STEM careers Apprenticeship opportunities Technical and vocational routes Higher education options The skills employers are looking for How their current studies connect to future careers 2. During Further Education Once young people are studying in FE, additional barriers can affect their ability to remain engaged and prepare for their next step. These may include: Financial hardship Transport costs Caring responsibilities Competing responsibilities outside education Low confidence Limited professional networks Limited access to role models Unmet special educational needs and disabilities Unmet mental health support needs Limited exposure to employers Lack of meaningful work experience These challenges can prevent young people from accessing opportunities that could improve their chances of entering STEM careers. 3. Exit from Further Education The transition out of FE can also be fragmented. Young people may leave college without having the employer connections, industry knowledge, work experience, careers support or confidence necessary to secure sustainable opportunities. This can increase the risk of young people becoming NEET — not in education, employment or training . The STEM Pathways Fund seeks to address these challenges by supporting organisations that can provide sustained transition support rather than relying on one-off interventions immediately before a young person leaves FE. What Does the Fund Aim to Achieve? The fund has two broad ambitions. First, it seeks to improve outcomes for young people. Second, it aims to contribute to a stronger and more equitable Further Education and employment system. The fund will primarily assess projects according to the outcomes they achieve for young people while also considering how projects can contribute to wider system change. Individual projects are not expected to transform the entire system on their own. However, applicants are expected to consider how their work can influence inclusive practices, sector priorities, policies, partnerships and approaches to supporting young people. Direct Outcomes for Young People Funded projects should contribute to meaningful improvements in young people s progression. Expected outcomes include: Better Understanding of STEM Pathways Young people should gain a stronger understanding of the different STEM routes available to them. This should help them make informed decisions about education, training and employment. Increased Confidence Projects should help young people develop greater confidence, skills and belief that STEM careers are accessible and relevant to people from their backgrounds. Greater Access to Opportunities Young people should have more equitable access to high-quality STEM opportunities, including: Employers Professional networks Mentors Role models Workplace experiences Work placements Internships Industry exposure Successful Progression Ultimately, projects should help young people successfully transition from Further Education into: STEM employment Apprenticeships Higher education Technical education Further STEM training Wider System Outcomes The fund also seeks to generate wider benefits for the FE and employment system. Funded projects can contribute to: Better understanding of the practical, financial and structural barriers affecting young people s STEM progression More equitable policy and practice Greater recognition of Further Education as a valuable pathway into STEM Better understanding of the support young people need to succeed Sharing evidence and learning about effective transition approaches Stronger collaboration between FE providers, STEM employers and community organisations Improved quality and accessibility of STEM transition opportunities How Much Funding Is Available? The STEM Pathways Fund will take a portfolio approach , meaning that it intends to support a small number of organisations working across England and fund different models of transition support. The fund anticipates awarding: Up to four grants £75,000 to £150,000 per grant Projects lasting up to 24 months The exact amount awarded to each successful organisation will depend on factors such as: Scope of the proposed project Ambition of the project Proposed activities Expected outcomes Project budget Organisational capacity Overall fit with the fund s objectives The funding is intended to be flexible and, where appropriate, unrestricted. This approach allows funded organisations to develop solutions that respond to their local circumstances while contributing to shared outcomes. Who Is the Fund Designed to Support? The fund focuses on organisations supporting young people aged 16–19 in Further Education settings across England who face barriers to progressing into STEM pathways. Particular groups include young people experiencing: Financial hardship Caring responsibilities Unmet Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Unmet mental health support needs Limited access to professional networks Limited access to STEM role models Limited access to workplace experiences Underrepresentation in STEM pathways Other systemic barriers affecting education and employment outcomes The fund specifically recognises that young people may experience multiple and intersecting barriers. Rather than simply categorising young people according to labels, the fund wants applicants to demonstrate an understanding of their communities actual experiences, challenges, strengths and aspirations. What STEM Careers and Pathways Are Covered? The fund takes a broad approach to STEM. STEM pathways are understood as routes that enable young people to progress into careers across science, technology, engineering and mathematics . The fund recognises that there is no single route into a STEM career. Young people may enter STEM through academic, technical, vocational or employment-based routes. Eligible pathways may include: STEM-related employment STEM apprenticeships Degree apprenticeships University degrees Higher technical qualifications Vocational STEM qualifications Further education Specialist STEM training programmes Recognised education, training or employment opportunities supporting progression towards STEM careers The fund is therefore not limited to traditional university-based STEM education. Projects that help young people understand the breadth of STEM opportunities and identify pathways appropriate to their interests, circumstances and aspirations are encouraged. What Does Transition Support Mean? The fund does not view transition support as a single intervention delivered immediately before a young person leaves FE. Instead, it believes effective transition support should be: Planned Sustained Personalised Collaborative Delivered over an appropriate period Where possible, support should begin at least one year before a young person is expected to progress into STEM employment, an apprenticeship, higher education or technical training. This means successful applicants are expected to demonstrate how their approach supports young people before, during and around critical transition points. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The fund is open to eligible not-for-profit organisations operating in England that work with young people aged 16–19 in Further Education. Eligible organisations include: Registered charities Charitable Incorporated Organisations (CIOs) Community Interest Companies (CICs) limited by guarantee Community Benefit Societies with an asset lock Cooperative Societies with an asset lock Other not-for-profit organisations with an asset lock Further Education Colleges Designated Sixth Form Colleges The fund does not accept applications from University Technical Colleges (UTCs). School sixth forms are also not eligible. The fund specifically refers to designated Sixth Form Colleges operating as independent Further Education institutions. Where applicable, organisations must have an asset lock ensuring that their assets and profits are used for community benefit. What Kind of Organisations Will Be Competitive? Eligible organisations should ideally be able to demonstrate practical experience in supporting young people aged 16–19 to progress into STEM pathways. Applicants should demonstrate: Experience working with young people Experience supporting progression into employment, apprenticeships, higher education or technical training Strong understanding of the Further Education environment Knowledge of the challenges faced by FE learners Understanding of the specific barriers experienced by the target groups Evidence that the proposed intervention responds to an identified need Capacity to deliver the proposed activities Meaningful relationships with relevant partners Organisations without extensive direct FE experience may still be able to apply where they can demonstrate a credible partnership with one or more FE colleges. Partnerships Are Strongly Encouraged The fund places significant emphasis on collaboration. Applications may be strengthened where organisations work alongside: Further Education colleges STEM employers Community organisations Young people Local partners Other organisations with relevant expertise The purpose is not to duplicate existing FE provision but to strengthen it. A strong partnership could combine the expertise of an FE college, the industry access of STEM employers and the specialist experience of a community organisation working directly with disadvantaged young people. Organisations Outside London Are Particularly Encouraged The fund specifically indicates that it would especially like to hear from organisations working outside London . It is also interested in: Smaller not-for-profit organisations Organisations with strong community relationships Organisations that collaborate with young people in designing their services Ethnic minority-led organisations Collaborative partnerships bringing together different forms of expertise The fund recognises the value of lived experience and local knowledge in designing effective interventions. What Is an Ethnic Minority-Led Organisation? For this particular fund, an ethnic minority-led organisation is defined as one where: The Chief Executive Officer or equivalent, or Chair of the Board, self-identifies as being from an ethnic minority background; and At least 50% of the Board of Trustees/Management Committee and/or senior leadership team also self-identify as being from an ethnic minority background. Collaborations involving ethnic minority-led organisations are particularly welcomed where they bring important lived expertise to the work. What Will the STEM Pathways Fund Support? The fund is open to a range of activities that can strengthen successful transitions into STEM pathways. Potential activities include: Mentoring and Coaching Projects may provide young people with sustained mentoring, coaching and guidance from people who can help them understand and navigate STEM career pathways. STEM Role Models Young people may benefit from exposure to STEM professionals who can demonstrate the range of careers available and help challenge perceptions about who can succeed in STEM. Employer Engagement Projects can create meaningful relationships between young people and STEM employers. This could include: Employer talks Industry visits Career events Networking opportunities Employer-led workshops Industry mentoring Work Experience and Placements Applicants can propose practical experiences that allow young people to understand STEM workplaces and develop relevant skills. These could include: Work experience Placements Internships Workplace visits Employer projects Careers Education Projects may provide careers education that helps young people understand: Available STEM careers Entry requirements Qualifications Apprenticeships Technical routes University pathways Employer expectations Progression opportunities Confidence and Skills Development Funded activities can help young people develop confidence, employability skills and leadership capabilities required to progress. Collaborative Transition Models Organisations can develop collaborative approaches involving FE providers, employers, community organisations and young people. The fund also welcomes innovative approaches that can improve transitions into STEM pathways. What Will Not Be Funded? Applicants should carefully consider the fund s exclusions before submitting an Expression of Interest. The fund will not support: Capital costs, including building work and renovations Spending that has already taken place Activities taking place outside England Party political lobbying activities The practice or promotion of religion or particular belief systems Loan repayments Investment Projects should therefore focus on eligible programme activity and future delivery rather than retrospective expenditure or capital development. Does the Project Have to Be New? No. The fund welcomes both new and existing work . An existing programme can be considered where the organisation can demonstrate how the funding would: Strengthen the programme Expand its reach Enhance existing provision Improve outcomes Develop new partnerships Improve STEM transition pathways Applicants should clearly explain what the funding will enable them to achieve that they could not achieve through their existing resources. Application Process The application process has two stages. Stage 1: Expression of Interest The first stage is an Expression of Interest (EOI) . Applicants will provide information about: Their organisation The communities they serve The needs they have identified The barriers young people face Their proposed approach How the approach aligns with the fund s priorities The online EOI is expected to take approximately 45–60 minutes to complete. Only organisations that meet the eligibility requirements and demonstrate a strong fit with the fund s objectives will progress. Stage 2: Full Application A small number of organisations shortlisted through the EOI stage will be invited to submit a full application. The full application will provide an opportunity to give more detail about: The proposed project Delivery approach Project activities Expected impact Project budget Organisational capacity Due diligence information The project proposal will have a maximum length of five A4 pages . The full application builds on information submitted during the EOI stage, meaning shortlisted applicants will generally only be asked to provide additional information needed to support the funding decision. Assessment and Decision-Making Eligible applications will be reviewed by: Mission 44 Santander UK Foundation Mission 44 Youth Advisors The inclusion of Youth Advisors reflects the fund s participatory approach to decision-making. Shortlisted applicants may be contacted if additional information is required before a final funding decision is made. Important Application Dates and Deadline Applicants should pay close attention to the following timeline: Stage Date Expression of Interest opens Tuesday, 28 July 2026 Expression of Interest deadline Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM Invitation to submit full application Monday, 28 September 2026 Full application deadline Monday, 19 October 2026 at midday Funding decision Late November 2026 Grants awarded and activity begins December 2026 – January 2027 Expected programme delivery commencement January 2027 Main Deadline The Expression of Interest deadline is Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM. Organisations should not wait until the final day to prepare their EOI, particularly because they need to demonstrate eligibility, local need, organisational experience and alignment with the fund s objectives. Accessibility Support The EOI is submitted through a Google Form designed to make the process straightforward and proportionate. Applicants who experience accessibility barriers when completing the application can contact the fund team at: youth@mission44.org Visit the Mission 44 website HERE Who Should Consider Applying? This opportunity could be particularly relevant to organisations that already work with disadvantaged young people in Further Education and want to strengthen their STEM progression programmes. Potential applicants include organisations that: Operate on a not-for-profit basis Work with 16–19-year-olds Operate in England Work directly with Further Education learners Have established relationships with FE colleges Work with STEM employers Provide careers or employability support Deliver mentoring or coaching programmes Provide work experience or placements Support underrepresented groups in STEM Have evidence of barriers affecting local young people Can demonstrate measurable progression outcomes Organisations considering applying should carefully assess their legal status and operational location before investing significant time in the application. What Makes a Strong Application? Although funding decisions will depend on the overall assessment process, applicants should pay particular attention to several areas. Demonstrate a Clear Need Do not simply state that young people face barriers. Use evidence to demonstrate what those barriers look like in the communities you serve. Useful evidence may include: Local data FE learner insights Employer feedback Surveys Interviews Focus groups Existing programme data Lived experience Evidence from partner organisations Explain Why Your Approach Is Appropriate Applicants should clearly connect the identified problem with their proposed activities. For example, if young people lack access to STEM employers, explain how employer engagement, workplace visits or mentoring will address that gap. Show Strong FE Knowledge The fund places considerable importance on understanding the Further Education environment. Applicants should demonstrate that they understand: How FE learners experience transitions The pressures affecting FE institutions The needs of disadvantaged learners Existing support available Gaps in current provision How their project will complement rather than duplicate existing services Demonstrate Collaboration Strong partnerships can increase the reach and effectiveness of a project. Applicants should consider how FE colleges, STEM employers, community organisations and young people themselves can contribute to the design and delivery of the project. Involve Young People The fund values organisations that work collaboratively with young people to inform or influence their activities, programmes or services. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how young people have contributed to programme design or how they will have a meaningful voice during implementation. Focus on Sustainable Progression The ultimate objective is not simply participation in activities. Applicants should demonstrate how their project will help young people progress towards meaningful destinations such as: STEM employment Apprenticeships Degree apprenticeships Higher education Technical qualifications STEM training Why This Funding Opportunity Matters The STEM Pathways Fund is significant because it addresses a challenge that goes beyond simply encouraging young people to study STEM subjects. For many disadvantaged young people, the problem is not necessarily a lack of ambition. It can be a lack of access. Without professional networks, employers, mentors, role models, work experience and reliable careers guidance, young people may struggle to translate their interests and qualifications into real opportunities. The fund therefore takes a broader approach to STEM progression by recognising the importance of sustained transition support. It also recognises that different young people require different forms of support. A student experiencing financial hardship may need help accessing workplace opportunities. Another young person may require mentoring and confidence-building. Someone with caring responsibilities may require a more flexible progression model. The strongest approaches are likely to be those that understand these individual and intersecting barriers and respond to them appropriately. Key Facts at a Glance Fund: STEM Pathways Fund Category: Grant Lead organisations: Mission 44 and Santander UK Foundation Geographic scope: England only Primary beneficiaries: Young people aged 16–19 in Further Education Funding: £75,000–£150,000 per grant Number of anticipated grants: Up to four Maximum project duration: 24 months EOI opens: 28 July 2026 EOI deadline: 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM Full application deadline: 19 October 2026 at midday Expected programme start: January 2027 Application process: Two stages Eligible applicants: Eligible not-for-profit organisations and qualifying FE institutions operating in England UTCs: Not eligible School sixth forms: Not eligible Activities outside England: Not eligible Eligibility Summary: Who Qualifies? Eligible applicant category: Not-for-profit organisations and eligible Further Education institutions operating in England. Examples of eligible organisations: Registered charities, CIOs, CICs limited by guarantee, qualifying community benefit societies, qualifying cooperative societies, other not-for-profits with an asset lock, Further Education Colleges and designated Sixth Form Colleges. Target beneficiaries: Young people aged 16–19 studying in Further Education in England who experience barriers to progressing into STEM education, training or employment. Countries/regions eligible to apply: England only. This is not an international grant open to organisations from Ghana, other African countries, or other countries outside England. Race/ethnicity: The fund is open to eligible organisations serving the target groups in England. It particularly welcomes collaborations involving ethnic minority-led organisations and recognises the value of lived experience. It is not presented as a grant restricted exclusively to applicants of a particular race or ethnicity. Academic qualifications: The fund is not structured as an individual scholarship or academic award, so there is no stated minimum degree, diploma or academic qualification for individual applicants. Eligibility is primarily based on the applicant organisation s legal status, location, experience, target beneficiaries and alignment with the fund s objectives. Conclusion The STEM Pathways Fund 2026 offers a substantial opportunity for eligible organisations in England to strengthen the transition from Further Education into STEM careers, apprenticeships, higher education and technical training. With grants of £75,000 to £150,000 available for projects lasting up to 24 months , the fund provides significant scope for organisations to develop or expand programmes focused on mentoring, employer engagement, work experience, careers education, confidence building, skills development and collaborative progression support. The opportunity is particularly relevant to organisations working with young people who face financial, social, educational, structural or other barriers to STEM progression. Applicants should focus on demonstrating a clear understanding of the local challenges, strong relationships with Further Education providers and STEM employers, meaningful involvement of young people, and a credible pathway from project activities to measurable progression outcomes. The first and most important deadline is Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 5:00 PM , when Expressions of Interest close. Organisations that successfully pass the EOI stage will be invited to submit a more detailed full application. For eligible organisations in England, this fund represents an opportunity not only to secure significant financial support but also to contribute to a more inclusive STEM pipeline and help young people access opportunities that may otherwise remain out of reach. title: AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026: AISMA and UNIDO Invite Nominations for African Excellence in Industry 4.0
summary: The AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026 are calling for nominations from innovators, researchers, entrepreneurs, industrial leaders, and other technology-focused professionals contributing to Africa s digital and industrial transformation. The awards are organised by the Alliance for I4.0 and Smart Manufacturing in Africa (AISMA) with the support of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) . The 2026 edition marks the second edition of the AFRICA 4.0 Awards and will be held in Dakar, Senegal, in November 2026 . The awards seek to recognise African excellence in smart manufacturing, technological innovation, applied research, digital transformation, industrial leadership, and inclusive participation in Industry 4.0 . For innovators and researchers working on technologies such as artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, robotics, automation, additive manufacturing, digital twins, and data analytics, the awards provide an opportunity to have impactful work recognised within Africa s growing Industry 4.0 ecosystem. What Are the AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026? The AFRICA 4.0 Awards are designed to celebrate individuals, teams, and organisations contributing to the advancement of Industry 4.0 in Africa . Industry 4.0 refers broadly to the integration of advanced digital technologies into industrial and manufacturing processes. These technologies can help industries become more productive, connected, efficient, innovative, and sustainable. The 2026 awards recognise different dimensions of this transformation, ranging from technological innovation and academic research to industrial digitalisation and women s leadership. The initiative is aligned with broader efforts to promote Africa s industrial transformation through technology, partnerships, and sustainable growth. Four AFRICA 4.0 Awards Categories Nominations are being accepted across four major award categories, each targeting a different aspect of Africa s Industry 4.0 transformation. 1. Technological Innovation in Industry 4.0 This category recognises practical technological solutions that use advanced technologies to modernise African industries. Eligible innovations may incorporate technologies such as: Artificial intelligence (AI) Internet of Things (IoT) Robotics Industrial automation Additive manufacturing Digital twins Data analytics Other Industry 4.0 technologies The category is intended for solutions that demonstrate practical potential to improve industrial processes, productivity, efficiency, or competitiveness. Potential nominees include the following: Startups Small and medium-sized enterprises Research teams Innovation laboratories Industrial technology providers Applicants in this category should be able to demonstrate the technological innovation behind their project as well as its broader impact and potential for expansion. 2. Young Researcher in Industry 4.0 The Young Researcher in Industry 4.0 category focuses on promising African research contributing to industrial modernisation and the development of smart manufacturing processes. The award is particularly relevant to researchers whose work demonstrates potential for applied technology transfer and practical industrial application. Eligible candidates may include: Master s researchers PhD researchers Postdoctoral researchers Young university faculty members Research teams led by young scientists Research may address smart manufacturing, industrial technology, digital transformation, or other areas contributing to Africa s Industry 4.0 development. The category provides an opportunity for emerging African researchers to showcase research that could contribute to solving industrial challenges and accelerating technological adoption across the continent. 3. Digital Leadership Industrial Transformation This category recognises successful implementation of digital transformation within industrial and manufacturing environments. Rather than focusing solely on the development of a new technology, the category highlights demonstrated leadership and results in applying digital solutions to transform industrial operations. Potential nominees include the following: Industrial companies Manufacturing SMEs Public agencies Digital transformation leaders Industrial clusters Nominees should demonstrate how digital transformation has contributed to improvements within an industrial or manufacturing setting. This could include the adoption of digital technologies, modernisation of production processes, improved efficiency, stronger data use, or other forms of industrial transformation. 4. Women in Industry 4.0 in Africa The Women in Industry 4.0 in Africa category celebrates women making significant contributions to technology-driven industrial transformation. It recognises leadership, research, innovation, and entrepreneurship that contribute to a more inclusive and gender-balanced Industry 4.0 ecosystem across Africa. Potential nominees include the following: Women researchers Women entrepreneurs Engineers Executives Founders Innovators Project leaders The category highlights the importance of women s participation in Africa s technological and industrial future and recognises women who are helping to advance innovation and digital transformation across the continent. What Do Nominees Need to Demonstrate? The nomination process asks candidates to provide detailed information about the project, research, or initiative being put forward for consideration. Applicants will be required to provide information covering several important areas, including: Project Title Nominees must provide the title of the project they are currently working on. The title should clearly identify the project or initiative being submitted for consideration. Project Description Applicants must describe their project in a maximum of 300 words . This section should provide a clear explanation of what the project does, the problem it addresses, and its relevance to Industry 4.0 and Africa s industrial transformation. Technological Innovation or Research Nominees must describe the technological innovation or research component of their project. This section should explain the technology, research approach, or innovative concept underpinning the project. Depending on the award category, applicants may discuss areas such as Artificial intelligence Robotics IoT Automation Digital manufacturing Data analytics Digital twins Applied research Technology transfer Other relevant Industry 4.0 technologies Socio-Environmental and Economic Impact Applicants must also explain the socio-environmental and economic impact of their project. This is an important part of the nomination because it allows nominees to demonstrate how their work goes beyond technology itself and contributes to broader development outcomes. Nominees should clearly communicate the benefits or changes generated by their project where applicable. Current Stage of the Project The application requires nominees to indicate the current stage of their project. This allows the award organisers to understand the level of development or implementation that has already been achieved. Scalability Potential Nominees must explain the scalability potential of their project. In particular, applicants should explain how the innovation, research, or solution could potentially be Replicated Expanded Adapted Introduced in other locations Applied to additional industrial challenges Demonstrating scalability can help show the broader relevance and potential contribution of a project to Africa s industrial transformation. AFRICA 4.0 Awards Supporting Documents Applicants are required to upload their supporting materials in one PDF document . The application instructions specify that a missing document may result in the nomination not being considered for the award. The required documents include: Motivation letter Recommendation Letter 1 Recommendation Letter 2 CV Additional supporting materials The combined supporting document must be uploaded as a single PDF, with a maximum file size of 10 MB . Two Letters of Recommendation Are Required One of the key requirements is that nominees must be endorsed by at least two recognised researchers or industry leaders through letters of support and motivation. Applicants should therefore identify appropriate referees who are familiar with their work and are able to provide credible support for their nomination. The recommendation letters should ideally reinforce the nominee s: Expertise Research or innovation achievements Industry contribution Leadership Impact Potential for wider application or scalability Candidates should ensure that both recommendation letters are included in the single PDF submission together with the other required documents. Other Information Required in the Application The nomination form requests a range of personal, professional, and project-related information. Applicants will be asked to provide: First name and last name Age Gender Citizenship Email address Current position Country of residence Award category Project title Project description Description of technological innovation or research Socio-environmental and economic impact Current stage of the project Scalability potential The form also asks applicants whether they have previously received any awards related to Industry 4.0. Nominees will also be asked how they heard about the AFRICA 4.0 Awards, with options including the AISMA website, LinkedIn, email, friends, or other sources. Applicants must confirm that the information they provide is accurate and agree to be contacted by AISMA regarding their nomination. The form also includes a consent option allowing AISMA and UNIDO to use the applicant s information to share the latest news and offers, with an option to unsubscribe. AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026 Timeline Applicants should take note of the key dates associated with the 2026 awards. Submission Deadline 30 September 2026 This is the deadline for submitting nominations for consideration. Finalists Selection 15 October 2026 The selection of finalists is scheduled for 15 October 2026. Award Ceremony November 2026 The award ceremony will take place in Dakar, Senegal , as part of the second edition of the AFRICA 4.0 Awards. Candidates should therefore plan their applications early, particularly because the nomination requires multiple supporting documents and two recommendation letters. Who Can Benefit From the AFRICA 4.0 Awards? The awards are particularly relevant to individuals, research teams, startups, SMEs, companies, and organisations contributing to Industry 4.0 and digital industrial transformation in Africa. Depending on the category, potential nominees include the following: African technology innovators Startup founders Entrepreneurs SMEs Industrial technology providers Researchers Master s students PhD candidates Postdoctoral researchers Young faculty members Research teams Engineers Digital transformation leaders Industrial companies Manufacturing companies Public agencies Industrial clusters Women innovators Women entrepreneurs Women researchers Women executives Women founders Project leaders Applicants should select the award category that most closely matches the nature of their work and ensure that the project demonstrates a meaningful connection to Industry 4.0, industrial transformation, technological innovation, research, or inclusive leadership. Why the AFRICA 4.0 Awards Matter Africa s industrial future is increasingly connected to the adoption of advanced technologies. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, IoT, and data analytics have the potential to transform how African industries manufacture products, manage resources, collect and use information, and compete in regional and global markets. The AFRICA 4.0 Awards provide a platform for recognising individuals and organisations contributing to this transformation. The awards also highlight that Industry 4.0 is not limited to large multinational companies. Startups, SMEs, researchers, universities, innovation laboratories, entrepreneurs, and individual technology leaders can all play important roles in developing solutions suited to African industrial realities. By recognising innovation, research, digital leadership, and women s participation, the awards cover several dimensions of Africa s emerging technology and manufacturing ecosystem. AFRICA 4.0 Conference 2026 The awards are connected to the broader AFRICA 4.0 Conference 2026 , organised by AISMA with the support of UNIDO and in partnership with AUDA-NEPAD . The conference brings together key stakeholders to advance Africa s industrial transformation through: Technology Partnerships Innovation Sustainable growth The conference provides a broader platform for stakeholders interested in Africa s industrial and technological transformation, while the awards specifically recognise outstanding contributions within the Industry 4.0 ecosystem. How to Prepare a Strong AFRICA 4.0 Awards Nomination Although the nomination form provides specific questions, applicants can strengthen their submissions by presenting their projects clearly and demonstrating their real-world relevance. A strong nomination should clearly explain: 1. The problem being addressed Explain the industrial, technological, economic, social, or environmental challenge that the project seeks to solve. 2. The innovation or research Clearly describe what makes the project innovative, technologically significant, or research-driven. 3. The Industry 4.0 connection Show how the project relates to technologies or approaches associated with Industry 4.0. 4. The impact Explain the project s socio-environmental and economic contribution and, where possible, demonstrate concrete results. 5. The project s development stage Clearly communicate whether the project is at the research, prototype, pilot, implementation, or expansion stage, based on the project s actual status. 6. Scalability Explain how the project could be replicated or expanded beyond its current application. 7. Supporting evidence Use the additional supporting materials to demonstrate achievements, results, research outputs, partnerships, implementation evidence, or other relevant accomplishments. 8. Strong recommendations Select recognised researchers or industry leaders who can provide meaningful and credible endorsements of the nominee and their work. APPLY HERE Important Application Considerations Applicants should carefully review their nomination before submission. In particular, candidates should ensure that: They have selected the correct award category. Their project description does not exceed the stated 300-word limit. All required supporting documents are included. Both recommendation letters are attached. The CV is included. Additional supporting materials are included where relevant. All documents are combined into one PDF. The PDF does not exceed the 10 MB upload limit. Personal and project information is accurate. The nomination is submitted before the deadline of 30 September 2026. Because the application states that a missing document can lead to a nomination not being considered, candidates should carefully check their submission before completing the form. Visit HERE for more information about the AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026. Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026 Organiser AISMA Support UNIDO Edition Second edition Location of Award Ceremony Dakar, Senegal Award Focus Industry 4.0, smart manufacturing, digital transformation, research and inclusive leadership Award Categories Four Submission Deadline 30 September 2026 Finalists Selection 15 October 2026 Award Ceremony November 2026 Project Description Limit Maximum 300 words Required Recommendations Two letters Supporting Document Format Single PDF Maximum File Size 10 MB Conclusion The AFRICA 4.0 Awards 2026 offer a significant platform for recognising African innovators, researchers, entrepreneurs, industrial leaders, and organisations contributing to the continent s Industry 4.0 transformation. With four award categories covering technological innovation, young research, digital leadership, and women s participation in Industry 4.0 , the awards provide opportunities for different actors within Africa s technology and industrial ecosystem to showcase their work and achievements. The nomination process requires applicants to provide detailed information about their project, including its technological or research component, socio-environmental and economic impact, current stage of development, and potential for scalability. Nominees must also submit a motivation letter, two recommendation letters, a CV, and any additional supporting materials in a single PDF of no more than 10 MB. The submission deadline is 30 September 2026 , followed by finalist selection on 15 October 2026 and the award ceremony in November 2026 in Dakar, Senegal . For African innovators, researchers, and industry leaders working to use technology to build more productive, inclusive, and sustainable industries, the AFRICA 4.0 Awards provide an opportunity to bring visibility to solutions and research that can contribute to the continent s next phase of industrial development. For more global Award opportunities, visit OFY HERE. title: Safeguarding Consultant Jobs in Southeast Asia 2026: Cowater International Opens Regional Safeguarding Roster
summary: Cowater International is inviting qualified safeguarding professionals to join its Safeguarding Roster of Consultants for Southeast Asia , an opportunity focused on strengthening organisational safeguarding systems among organisations working to prevent gender-based violence (GBV) across the region. The consultancy is part of the Southeast Asia Gender-based Violence Prevention Platform , a regionally led and Australian-funded initiative designed to increase investment, coordination, evidence-based practice, advocacy, and capacity for the primary prevention of gender-based violence against women and girls across Southeast Asia. The position offers experienced safeguarding specialists an opportunity to provide technical assistance to civil society organisations, women s rights organisations and other local partners while contributing to stronger safeguarding policies, systems, and practices across the region. About the Southeast Asia Gender-Based Violence Prevention Platform The Southeast Asia Gender-Based Violence Prevention Platform was established in response to the need for greater investment and coordination in gender-based violence primary prevention initiatives across Southeast Asia. The initiative is built around a shared commitment to ending gender-based violence against women and girls in all their diversity. It seeks to strengthen locally led approaches by promoting evidence-based advocacy, dialogue, policy development, and programming. The Platform is led by a regionally based Secretariat and works in collaboration with Cowater International, Social Development Direct and the Equality Institute . These collaborating organisations provide organisational development and technical assistance to support the Platform s work. The programme operates through three major pillars: 1. Demonstrate This pillar focuses on generating and sharing evidence about what works in preventing gender-based violence in Southeast Asia. The objective is to ensure that evidence on effective GBV prevention approaches is accessible and applied by practitioners and policymakers across the region. 2. Advocate The Advocate pillar seeks to expand regional and bilateral cooperation among multiple stakeholders working on GBV prevention. It aims to strengthen collaboration and commitment to gender-based violence prevention among governments, organisations, practitioners, policymakers, and other relevant stakeholders. 3. Facilitate The Facilitate pillar is designed to strengthen the capacity of practitioners and policymakers to develop, implement, and monitor high-quality, evidence-based GBV prevention policies and programmes. The Platform also provides competitive grants to civil society organisations and women s rights organisations in Southeast Asia. These grants are offered through several funding cycles and range from AUD 20,000 to AUD 150,000 . About the Safeguarding Consultant Position The Safeguarding Consultant will provide tailored technical assistance to a portfolio of Platform grantees to help them strengthen their organisational safeguarding systems and practices. The work is intended to ensure that participating organisations operate in accordance with DFAT safeguarding standards and the safeguarding standards established by the Platform. The consultant will work under the overall guidance of the Platform s Safeguarding Specialist, with technical support from the Safeguarding Adviser of the Technical Partner. Rather than simply producing safeguarding documents for organisations, the consultant will act as a technical partner throughout the grant lifecycle. The approach is intended to help organisations build sustainable safeguarding capacity based on their existing systems, strengths, risks, and organisational context. Key Responsibilities of the Safeguarding Consultant Successful consultants will be expected to undertake responsibilities across grant assessment, safeguarding planning, technical assistance, monitoring, and coordination. Grant Assessment and Onboarding At the beginning of the grant process, the consultant will contribute to safeguarding-related assessment and onboarding activities. Key responsibilities include: Providing technical input into the safeguarding review of grant applications. Supporting due diligence processes. Contributing to safeguarding risk assessments. Helping identify safeguarding risks associated with proposed projects. Recommending appropriate measures for mitigating identified risks. Helping grantees understand DFAT safeguarding standards. Ensuring grantees understand their safeguarding responsibilities throughout the grant period. This means candidates should be comfortable assessing organisational risks and translating safeguarding standards into practical requirements that local organisations can understand and implement. Safeguarding Action Planning Another major responsibility will involve helping grantees develop and strengthen their safeguarding action plans. The consultant will be expected to: Review safeguarding policies, procedures, and supporting organisational documents. Assess existing organisational safeguarding capacity. Compare existing systems against DFAT and Platform safeguarding standards. Facilitate the development or refinement of risk-proportionate Safeguarding Action Plans. Build on the organisation s existing safeguarding systems, strengths, and priorities. Help grantees identify realistic and achievable safeguarding priorities. Ensure agreed priorities are aligned with relevant DFAT standards and expectations. The emphasis is therefore not on imposing a standardised safeguarding model. Instead, consultants are expected to help organisations strengthen systems that are appropriate to their specific circumstances and levels of risk. Ongoing Technical Assistance and Capacity Strengthening The successful consultant will provide continuing technical support throughout the grant lifecycle. This may include: Providing tailored safeguarding advice and technical accompaniment. Reviewing safeguarding policies and procedures. Providing feedback on safeguarding tools and resources developed by grantees. Supporting organisations to operationalise safeguarding systems. Strengthening reporting mechanisms. Supporting risk management processes. Advising on safe recruitment practices. Supporting safeguarding training and governance. Delivering or facilitating safeguarding learning sessions. Providing coaching or mentoring where necessary. Working with grantees, mentors, mentees, and other Platform partners. Identifying emerging safeguarding concerns. Working with the Platform Secretariat to develop appropriate responses to emerging issues. The position therefore requires more than theoretical knowledge of safeguarding. Candidates need to demonstrate an ability to work directly with organisations, understand their practical challenges, and help them implement workable solutions. Monitoring, Documentation, and Coordination The consultant will also be responsible for following up on safeguarding progress and maintaining effective communication with assigned organisations. Responsibilities include: Maintaining regular communication with grantees. Monitoring progress against agreed Safeguarding Action Plans. Documenting progress and emerging challenges. Recording agreed next steps and technical assistance provided. Identifying situations where safeguarding priorities or action plans need to change as projects evolve. Escalating complex safeguarding concerns, incidents, or significant organisational risks to the Platform Safeguarding Specialist. Ensuring that technical advice remains consistent with DFAT safeguarding requirements and Platform guidance. A Facilitative and Locally Led Approach One of the most important aspects of this consultancy is the expected working approach. Consultants are expected to use a facilitative, collaborative, and capacity-strengthening approach . Rather than taking over the safeguarding responsibilities of partner organisations or simply writing policies on their behalf, consultants should help organisations develop and implement their own safeguarding systems. This makes experience in organisational development, mentoring, coaching, and locally led development particularly relevant. Candidates should therefore be able to work respectfully with different types of organisations and support them to build on their existing strengths and systems. Qualifications Required for the Safeguarding Consultant Role Educational Requirements Applicants should have at least a Bachelor s degree in a relevant discipline. Acceptable fields include: Social work Gender and development International development Community development Human rights Social sciences Another relevant field A postgraduate qualification is desirable but not essential . Additional training or professional certification can strengthen an application. The position particularly values training or certification in areas such as the following: Safeguarding Child protection Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH) Gender-based violence Protection Investigations Related safeguarding fields Professional Experience Requirements Candidates must have a minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in safeguarding, child protection, PSEAH, gender-based violence, or related areas. Importantly, this experience should include providing technical assistance, organisational capacity strengthening, or safeguarding support to: Civil society organisations NGOs Development partners Women s rights organisations Community-based organisations Other local partners Specific Skills and Experience Applicants should be able to demonstrate experience in developing, reviewing, and strengthening organisational safeguarding systems. Relevant experience includes: Developing and reviewing safeguarding policies. Strengthening safeguarding procedures. Developing or reviewing codes of conduct. Establishing reporting mechanisms. Strengthening case-handling mechanisms. Developing safeguarding prevention and response systems. Conducting safeguarding risk assessments. Developing risk mitigation measures. Implementing and monitoring risk mitigation measures. Providing technical assistance and mentoring. Facilitating safeguarding training and workshops. Providing safeguarding coaching and organisational mentoring. Candidates should also have a strong understanding of: Safeguarding principles. Victim-survivor-centred approaches. Child safeguarding. PSEAH. International donor safeguarding standards. DFAT safeguarding requirements or comparable standards. Locally led development principles. Interpersonal and Professional Competencies The role requires strong interpersonal and analytical abilities because consultants will work with organisations that may have different levels of safeguarding capacity and different operational contexts. Applicants should demonstrate: Strong analytical skills. Excellent facilitation skills. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. The ability to explain complex safeguarding concepts in practical and accessible language. Sound professional judgement. The ability to maintain confidentiality. The ability to manage sensitive safeguarding information with professionalism and integrity. Experience working with diverse organisations is also highly desirable. This includes experience with women s rights organisations, organisations of persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ groups, and other organisations representing or supporting different communities. Language Requirements Applicants must have proficiency in English and at least one Southeast Asian language , both written and oral. This requirement is important because the consultant will work with organisations and stakeholders across Southeast Asia and will need to communicate technical safeguarding concepts effectively in relevant local contexts. Who Can Apply? The opportunity has a specific geographic eligibility requirement. It is open to citizens of the following Southeast Asian countries : Brunei Darussalam Cambodia Indonesia Lao PDR Malaysia Myanmar The Philippines Singapore Thailand Timor-Leste Viet Nam Applicants must be based in and legally authorised to work in the country concerned . The organisation states that applications from citizens of other regions or countries will not be considered and that it cannot issue a working visa for this purpose. Diversity and Equal Opportunity The opportunity places emphasis on diversity, inclusion, gender equality, and intersectionality. Women in all their diversity, persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and people from historically marginalised or underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply. The organisation also states that it is committed to hiring based on merit and qualifications and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, sex, gender identity, disability, age, or other legally protected grounds. Application Deadline Deadline: 28 August 2026 at 17:00 Bangkok/Jakarta time (GMT+7). Candidates interested in the opportunity should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated deadline and meet the specified eligibility and documentation requirements. How to Apply Applicants are required to submit application documents that demonstrate their suitability for the Safeguarding Consultant position. The application should include: 1. Updated CV The CV should clearly highlight relevant safeguarding experience, professional achievements, qualifications, and technical expertise in relation to the requirements of the consultancy. Applicants should particularly emphasise experience in: Safeguarding system strengthening. GBV prevention. Child protection. PSEAH. Risk assessment. Safeguarding policy development. title: 2027 Hoover Fellows Program at Stanford University
summary: The Hoover Institution at Stanford University is seeking outstanding early-career scholars for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program , an opportunity for researchers whose work has implications for public policy. Hoover Fellows will be based at the Hoover Institution in Stanford, California , where they will have the opportunity to pursue scholarly research, publish academic work, and contribute to the intellectual life of one of Stanford University s leading research centers. The fellowship is particularly suited to scholars working in fields such as economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, and public policy. According to the 2027 opportunity information provided by the Hoover Institution, appointments are for one to three years , and the position carries no teaching responsibilities . About the Hoover Fellows Program The Hoover Institution is a research center at Stanford University focused on research and scholarship with relevance to public policy. Hoover scholars contribute to research and intellectual discussions on issues including economics, national security, international relations, and governance. The Hoover Fellows Program provides early-career scholars with an opportunity to concentrate on their research and scholarly writing while participating in the intellectual community at Hoover and engaging with Stanford s broader research environment. During the fellowship, Fellows are expected to produce scholarly articles and books that have implications for public policy. They are also expected to contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution. Unlike some academic fellowships, the position does not include teaching responsibilities, allowing Fellows to focus primarily on research and publication. Fellowship Benefits The 2027 Hoover Fellow position offers a highly competitive compensation package. Salary Selected Fellows will receive a 12-month base salary ranging from $169,950 to $230,000 . Housing Allowance In addition to the base salary, Fellows will receive a $20,000 annual housing allowance . Research Environment Fellows will be based at the Hoover Institution on Stanford University s campus in Stanford, California. They will also be encouraged to engage with Stanford s wider research community in their respective fields. This provides Fellows with an opportunity to interact with scholars and researchers beyond Hoover while developing their own academic research agendas. Fellowship Duration The 2027 opportunity specifies an appointment term of one to three years . The position is based at the Hoover Institution, Stanford, California , and Fellows are expected to participate in the Institution s intellectual community while pursuing their research. Areas of Research The Hoover Fellows Program is open to scholars working in relevant academic and policy fields. Examples of eligible fields include: Economics History International Relations National Security Political Science Public Policy Applicants from related disciplines may also be considered where their research aligns with the Hoover Institution s mission and has meaningful implications for public policy. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must be early-career scholars who hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in a relevant field , or who expect to complete the degree by September 1, 2027 . The opportunity is therefore particularly relevant to doctoral candidates approaching completion of their Ph.D. as well as scholars who have already completed their doctoral studies. Applicants should have an academic and research background that demonstrates their potential to produce significant scholarly work. Candidates are expected to show how their research can contribute to broader discussions relevant to public policy. What Will Hoover Fellows Do? Selected Fellows will primarily focus on research and scholarly activities. During the fellowship, they are expected to: Conduct research in their area of specialization. Produce scholarly articles and other academic publications. Develop books or book-length research where appropriate. Pursue research projects with implications for public policy. Contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution. Engage with Stanford s broader research community. Participate in scholarly discussions connected to their research interests. Because the position carries no teaching responsibilities , Fellows can devote their time primarily to research, writing, and intellectual engagement. Application Requirements Applicants must submit several documents as part of their application. 1. Cover Letter or Statement of Interest Applicants should provide a cover letter or statement of interest describing their academic background and experience. This document should clearly communicate the applicant s research interests, academic preparation, and reasons for seeking the Hoover Fellowship. 2. Recent Scholarly Work Applicants must submit one or more recent publications, working papers, or draft book chapters . These materials allow the selection committee to assess the applicant s research quality, scholarly writing, and potential for future contributions. 3. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide an up-to-date CV outlining their academic background, research experience, publications, professional experience, awards, and other relevant achievements. 4. Future Research Statement Applicants must submit a statement describing their future research plans . The research statement must be no more than two pages and should clearly explain the research the applicant intends to pursue during the fellowship and its potential significance. 5. Three Letters of Recommendation Applicants are required to provide three letters of recommendation . The letters should address the candidate s research accomplishments and potential for future research. Applicants should therefore select recommenders who can provide meaningful assessments of their academic and research capabilities. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is particularly suitable for early-career researchers who are developing independent research programmes and want to work in a leading research environment. Potential applicants include: Ph.D. candidates nearing completion of their degrees. Recent Ph.D. graduates. Early-career scholars in economics and related disciplines. Researchers working on international relations and national security. Political scientists and historians. Public policy researchers. Scholars whose research has clear implications for public policy. Applicants should have a strong research profile and be prepared to demonstrate their potential for future scholarly contributions. Location The Hoover Fellows Program is based at: Hoover Institution Stanford University Stanford, California, USA The Hoover Institution is located in the heart of Stanford University s campus, providing Fellows with access to a broader academic and research environment. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program is: November 17, 2026 Time: 11:59 PM Pacific Time Applicants are encouraged to prepare their application materials well in advance of the deadline, particularly because the application requires three recommendation letters and several research documents. How to Apply Applications must be submitted online through the Hoover Institution s application platform. Application Portal: Apply for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program Applicants should ensure that all required documents and recommendation letters are submitted according to the instructions before the deadline. For questions about the fellowship, applicants can contact hooverfellowship@stanford.edu . The Hoover Institution notes that this inbox is checked only periodically. Important Information for Applicants Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should make sure they: Hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree, or expect to complete it by September 1, 2027. Have a research background in a relevant academic field. Prepare a strong cover letter or statement of interest. Include recent scholarly work, working papers, or a draft book chapter. Prepare an updated academic CV. Develop a focused future research statement of no more than two pages. Identify three appropriate referees. Allow enough time for recommendation letters to be submitted. Submit the complete application before November 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Why Consider the Hoover Fellowship? For early-career scholars, the fellowship provides an opportunity to dedicate substantial time to research and scholarly publication while becoming part of the intellectual community at the Hoover Institution. The combination of a competitive salary, housing allowance, research-focused responsibilities, and access to Stanford s broader scholarly environment makes the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers seeking to advance an academic or policy-oriented career. The fellowship can also provide a valuable platform for scholars whose research seeks to connect academic scholarship with important public policy questions. Conclusion The 2027 Hoover Fellows Program at Stanford University offers an exciting opportunity for early-career scholars to pursue research in a prestigious academic and policy research environment. Successful Fellows will be expected to produce high-quality scholarly work, contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution, and engage with Stanford s wider research community. The position offers a 12-month base salary of $169,950 to $230,000 , plus a $20,000 annual housing allowance , and carries no teaching responsibilities. Researchers in economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, public policy, and related fields who meet the doctoral degree requirement are encouraged to consider applying. title: Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at PNNL | Fully Funded Research Fellowship in the USA
summary: The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career scientists and engineers who are ready to pursue ambitious, independent research. The prestigious fellowship provides selected researchers with full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception at PNNL. Fellows have the opportunity to develop original research ideas, work with internationally recognised scientists, access advanced research capabilities, and contribute to discoveries addressing important scientific and national challenges. The programme is designed for the next generation of scientists and engineers who want to push the boundaries of research and development and produce work with the potential for world-recognised impact. What Is the Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship? The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is a postdoctoral research programme hosted by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. Named after renowned scientist Linus Pauling , the fellowship supports exceptional recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering. Unlike a conventional postdoctoral position where researchers may primarily work on an established project, the Linus Pauling Fellowship allows successful candidates to propose and pursue a major research project of their own design . Applicants are expected to develop a detailed and original research proposal explaining their research plans, objectives, methodology, and anticipated outcomes. The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for talented early-career researchers to demonstrate scientific independence while benefiting from PNNL s research environment and expertise. What Does the Fellowship Offer? Selected Linus Pauling Fellows receive full funding to pursue their proposed research at PNNL. The fellowship provides researchers with an opportunity to: Develop and conduct a major research project of their own conception. Work alongside internationally recognised researchers. Access state-of-the-art scientific and technological capabilities. Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions. Advance scientific knowledge in their chosen field. Contribute to research addressing pressing national concerns. Build their scientific and professional networks. Develop their independence as researchers. Work within one of the United States leading national laboratory environments. The programme is particularly suited to researchers who already have a strong research background and a clear vision for an ambitious postdoctoral project. Research Areas Applicants can propose research connected to PNNL s mission areas. The fellowship highlights four broad areas of research: 1. Scientific Discovery Researchers interested in fundamental and applied scientific discovery can develop projects aimed at expanding knowledge and creating new scientific capabilities. Projects may involve emerging scientific questions and approaches capable of generating significant discoveries. 2. Energy Resiliency Energy is one of PNNL s major research areas. Researchers can explore topics related to energy systems, energy technologies, resilience, sustainability, and other challenges associated with securing and transforming energy systems. 3. Data Science and Computing The fellowship also supports research involving data science and computing. This area can be relevant to researchers developing advanced computational methods, data-driven approaches, modelling techniques, artificial intelligence applications, and other computational research aligned with PNNL s mission. 4. National Security PNNL conducts research addressing important national security challenges. Applicants whose research interests align with this area may develop proposals addressing scientific and technological challenges relevant to national security. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for qualified recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering . Applicants must have completed, or be on track to complete, a PhD in a science or engineering field related to the mission areas of PNNL. The degree must be from an accredited college or university . For the 2027 fellowship, qualified candidates must have completed their PhD within the last three years or prior to the start of the fellowship . This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for early-career researchers who have recently completed doctoral studies or are approaching completion. International Applicants The fellowship is based at PNNL in the United States. Applicants should note that all PNNL staff must be able to demonstrate the legal right to work in the United States . Therefore, prospective international applicants should carefully review the employment and work-authorisation requirements before applying. Eligibility should not be assumed solely based on academic qualifications. What Makes the Fellowship Competitive? The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for researchers who can demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions to science and engineering. A strong application should therefore go beyond simply describing an existing research project. Applicants are expected to present an original research proposal that demonstrates: A clear and important research question. Strong scientific reasoning. Originality and innovation. A well-defined research approach. Potential scientific or technological impact. Alignment with PNNL s mission areas. Clear anticipated outcomes. The potential to advance research beyond existing approaches. The ability to demonstrate an independent research vision is an important aspect of the fellowship. Research Proposal One of the central components of the application is the research proposal. Applicants must submit a detailed proposal describing the research project they intend to undertake. The proposal should communicate the central research idea clearly and explain how the proposed work could contribute to scientific or technological advancement. Candidates should carefully consider the connection between their proposed research and PNNL s research priorities. Because the fellowship allows researchers to pursue projects of their own conception, applicants should use the proposal to demonstrate both their scientific expertise and their capacity for independent research. Mentoring and Research Environment Linus Pauling Fellows benefit from mentoring by internationally recognised researchers at PNNL. This provides fellows with the opportunity to work in an environment where they can receive guidance while developing their own research programme. The fellowship combines independent research with access to experienced scientists and advanced research infrastructure. This can be particularly valuable for researchers seeking to transition from doctoral research into more independent scientific leadership. About Pacific Northwest National Laboratory Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a U.S. national laboratory known for research and technological innovation in areas including energy, environment, science, and national security. PNNL conducts multidisciplinary research aimed at addressing complex scientific and societal challenges. The laboratory s research environment gives fellows the opportunity to work with researchers from different scientific and engineering disciplines and use advanced capabilities to pursue ambitious projects. Why Apply for the Linus Pauling Fellowship? The fellowship can be an important opportunity for researchers who want to establish themselves as independent scientists or engineers. Rather than simply joining an existing research programme, successful candidates can develop a significant research project based on their own scientific vision. The fellowship can help researchers: Strengthen their independent research profile. Develop a major original research project. Work with leading scientists. Access advanced laboratory capabilities. Expand their professional network. Gain experience conducting research in a national laboratory. Build a foundation for a long-term scientific career. Contribute to research with potential global impact. Application Deadline Applications for the 2027 Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship are open until: 15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time (PST). Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the stated deadline. How to Apply Interested candidates should apply through the official PNNL careers portal. Application Link: https://careers.pnnl.gov/jobs/11983?lang=en-us Applicants should review the official vacancy and fellowship information carefully for the complete application requirements, required documents, and current instructions. The official fellowship page is also available through PNNL: https://www.pnnl.gov/projects/linus-pauling-distinguished-postdoctoral-fellowship Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Because the fellowship is designed for researchers with the potential to generate world-recognised discoveries, applicants should dedicate significant attention to their research proposal. Demonstrate Alignment With PNNL Explain how the proposed research connects to one or more of PNNL s mission areas, including scientific discovery, energy resiliency, data science and computing, or national security. Present a Strong Research Plan The proposal should provide a logical pathway from the research question to the anticipated outcomes. Demonstrate Independence The fellowship is an opportunity to establish an independent research identity. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to formulate and lead an ambitious research programme. Review Eligibility Carefully Candidates should confirm that their PhD timing, academic field, work authorisation, and other requirements satisfy the official fellowship conditions before submitting an application. Important Information for Applicants Applicants should rely on the official PNNL fellowship and careers pages for the most current requirements. The opportunity is highly competitive, and meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection. Candidates should also ensure that their proposal and supporting materials accurately represent their academic background, research achievements, and proposed work. Conclusion The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering to pursue ambitious independent research at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory in the United States. Selected fellows receive full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception while benefiting from mentorship by internationally recognised researchers and access to PNNL s advanced scientific capabilities. With research opportunities spanning Scientific Discovery, Energy Resiliency, Data Science and Computing, and National Security , the fellowship is particularly suited to researchers with innovative ideas and the ambition to make significant contributions to their fields. Qualified candidates should begin preparing their research proposal and supporting application materials early. Applications close on 15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. PST .
